cogentanalytics-cogentanalytics:lever:bd.title: Automotive Technician
cogentanalytics-cogentanalytics:lever:bd.description: Primary Role Summary The Automotive Technician is responsible for diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining customer vehicles safely, efficiently, and in accordance with manufacturer and company standards. The Technician plays a critical role in delivering quality repairs, identifying additional service opportunities, and ensuring an exceptional customer experience. The Automotive Technician serves as the technical expert within the shop, providing accurate inspections, quality workmanship, and professional recommendations that support customer safety, vehicle reliability, and company profitability. Key Responsibilities 1. Vehicle Diagnostics & Repair Perform vehicle inspections and diagnostic testing. Identify mechanical, electrical, drivability, and performance issues. Diagnose root causes and recommend corrective actions. Perform repairs according to manufacturer specifications and company standards. Complete maintenance services including brakes, tires, alignments, oil changes, suspension, batteries, and other vehicle systems. Verify repairs through testing and quality control procedures. 2. Inspection & Customer Recommendations Perform comprehensive vehicle inspections. Identify maintenance and repair opportunities. Document inspection findings accurately. Communicate repair recommendations clearly to Service Advisors. Support customer safety and preventative maintenance programs. Assist in maximizing vehicle reliability and customer satisfaction. 3. Productivity & Workflow Management Maintain efficient work habits and productivity levels. Complete assigned work within established labor times. Manage workflow and prioritize assignments effectively. Support overall shop throughput and scheduling objectives. Minimize delays and operational bottlenecks. 4. Quality Control & Workmanship Ensure repairs are completed correctly the first time. Follow shop quality control procedures. Conduct final inspections and testing prior to vehicle release. Minimize comeback repairs and warranty work. Maintain high standards of workmanship and professionalism. 5. Safety, Equipment & Facility Care Follow OSHA, EPA, and company safety requirements. Utilize tools, lifts, and diagnostic equipment properly. Maintain a clean and organized work area. Properly handle and dispose of hazardous materials. Report damaged equipment and safety concerns immediately. Protect customer vehicles and company assets. 6. Documentation & Communication Complete repair order notes accurately and thoroughly. Document diagnostic findings, repairs performed, and recommendations. Communicate effectively with Service Advisors and management. Maintain accurate labor and time records. Participate in production meetings and training activities. 7. Continuous Improvement & Training Stay current with automotive technology and repair procedures. Participate in technical training and certification programs. Develop advanced diagnostic and repair skills. Support mentorship and knowledge sharing within the shop. Promote a culture of professionalism and continuous improvement.

jobgether-jobgether:lever:14fc695b-0dc9-.title: Head of Operations for eCom DTC brand
jobgether-jobgether:lever:14fc695b-0dc9-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Head of Operations for eCom DTC brand based in Switzerland. This is a high-impact operations leadership role within a fast-growing, 8-figure direct-to-consumer business. You will take ownership of the operating infrastructure that supports supply chain, inventory, fulfillment, systems, reporting, hiring, and execution. The role is designed for a hands-on builder who can turn operational complexity into clear processes, accountable ownership, and measurable performance. You will identify gaps, build SOPs, establish systems, recruit functional leaders, and create the structure needed for sustainable scale. A major focus will be transitioning day-to-day operational responsibility away from the Founder and toward a capable team of independent functional owners. You will work across distributed teams, vendors, agencies, manufacturers, and operational partners in a highly entrepreneurial environment. Success means building an organization that runs efficiently, solves problems proactively, and no longer depends on you for daily execution. Own end-to-end back-end operations, including supply chain, inventory planning, manufacturing relationships, 3PL and fulfillment, returns, vendor management, and agency coordination. Build and maintain scalable operating systems, processes, and SOPs, ensuring every recurring workflow has clear ownership, documentation, measurement, and accountability. Establish and maintain an operational knowledge base in Notion, continuously improving processes as the business grows and new needs emerge. Develop accurate inventory systems of record, purchase-order calendars, and processes that improve inventory visibility, planning, and stock availability. Build reliable reporting and a single source of truth for weekly leadership metrics, including inventory, stockouts, cost per order, channel and subscription revenue, vendor performance, and other operational KPIs. Create automated subscription and channel revenue reporting and develop a concise weekly operations scorecard for leadership decision-making. Establish vendor and agency scorecards to monitor performance, identify issues, and drive continuous improvement. Identify missing organizational functions, define roles and scorecards, lead recruitment, conduct screening, onboard new hires, and develop functional owners. Build a team of 4–6 functional leaders who can independently own their respective areas and operate without daily intervention. Create repeatable hiring pipelines, work-sample assessments, onboarding systems, and accountability mechanisms. Translate decisions into clear written specifications with defined owners, deadlines, and completion criteria, then follow through until execution is complete. Diagnose operational issues by tracing performance changes back to their underlying causes and implementing sustainable solutions. Continuously identify and resolve operational problems before they escalate into Founder-level issues. Build the infrastructure and organizational capability required to ultimately transition into broader COO-level responsibilities. Requirements At least 3 years of operations experience within a physical-product, e-commerce, or direct-to-consumer business. Experience operating within a high-growth environment, ideally supporting or helping scale a brand generating approximately $20M–$50M in annual revenue. Direct experience across multiple operational functions, including supply chain, inventory, 3PL/fulfillment, customer support operations, creative, and growth teams. Demonstrated experience building a department, function, operating system, hiring process, reporting infrastructure, or other business capability from the ground up. Strong understanding of physical-product operations, including lead times, purchase orders, landed costs, inventory, fulfillment, manufacturing, and 3PL relationships
